free_tier.stated: No free tier and no trial is published; the cheapest slot is USD 5/month for 50 GB.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: sold by total disk (50 GB, 100 GB, 200 GB); no single-file cap is published

retention.stated: for the life of the subscription; no inactivity deletion is stated

egress.terms: 'All plans come with unmetered bandwidth' and 'With unmetered bandwidth, we do not monitor your data transfers. But if you on a shared server, you will share the network with other users.' Download 1 Gbps, upload 300 Mbps per slot, 10-16 users per server.
egress.free_allowance: unmetered, bounded by a shared 300 Mbit/s upload

interface_detail: 'Secure FTP access - All FTP info included in the welcome email'; 'FTP with FXP support'; 'HTTP(S) download site - A private URL to your download folder'.
tooling: FTP/FTPS clients with FXP support (vendor names FlashFXP); ruTorrent with 30+ plugins; no rsync or API is documented
chaining: A USD 5 slot that moves files server-to-server over FXP and serves them over HTTP(S); unmetered, so the shared 300 Mbit/s upload and 10-16 co-tenants are what a 1 TiB pull actually fights

limits.value: public-tracker upload capped at 1 MB/s (8 Mbit/s) until ratio 1.0
300 Mbit/s upload shared by 10-16 users per server

limits_note: Retrieval is unmetered; the shaping applies to seeding on public trackers, and the shared 300 Mbit/s is the ceiling on what one slot can take from a busy server.
binding_note: No byte quota exists, so nothing in the vocabulary fails at 1 TiB/month. The practical limits are the 50 GB disk (20 cycles per TiB) and contention with 10-16 co-tenants, neither of which the vocabulary names.

identity_cost.detail: Account plus payment; no free tier. No phone or document check is stated.

reliability_note: Public-tracker upload is shaped to 1 MB/s until ratio 1.0, so a fresh account builds ratio slowly; unmetered transfers are shared with 10-16 users per server.
confidence_note: Prices, rates, protocols and the public-tracker shape are on the vendor's own home page and FAQ read. A measured rung needs a slot and a timed transfer.

evidence.proved: 50 GB at USD 5/m, 100 GB at USD 7/m, 200 GB at USD 10/m; 1 Gbps download, 300 Mbps upload; 10-16 users per Xeon E3-1220v2 server; 'Unlimited download speed, 1 MB/s (8 Mbps) upload until 1.0 ratio'
'Unmetered bandwidth ... we do not monitor your data transfers'; FXP and a private HTTP(S) download URL; unlimited active torrents

notes: Exactly USD 5, so it sits on the line rather than under it; the per-TB price is the worst and the 50 GB disk is the reason. Sustained-rate conversion: unmetered claim, so the comparable figure is the 300 Mbit/s shared upload, 37.5 MB/s aggregate across 10-16 users. The disk is first, the share second.

extras.apps: ruTorrent with 30+ plugins, OpenVPN on request, private HTTP(S) download site; no Plex or *arr is stated
